history.summary: The Birla Mandir of Hyderabad stands on the 280-ft Naubat Pahad hillock on a 13-acre plot near Khairatabad, overlooking Hussain Sagar. Built by the Birla Foundation over ten years (1966-1976), it was opened in 1976 by Swami Ranganathananda of the Ramakrishna Mission. The temple is constructed of some 2000 tons of white Rajasthani marble and blends Dravidian, Rajasthani and Utkala architecture (the gopuram in South Indian style, the Jagadananda Vimanam in Oriya style), with carved scenes from the Ramayana and Mahabharata and inscribed teachings of holy men and Gurbani on the walls. The sanctum replicates the Venkateswara shrine at Tirupati with an 11-ft granite idol of Lord Venkateswara under a carved lotus umbrella; a 42-ft brass flagstaff rises in the premises. The temple has no traditional bells, at Swami Ranganathananda's wish that the atmosphere be conducive to meditation. Note: sources consulted do not document a major annual festival for this temple - festivals left empty rather than invented. Free entry; shoes removed and phones kept in lockers at the base (verify on visit).

name: Birla Mandir
town_description: Naubat Pahad is a 280-ft (85 m) granite hillock in central Hyderabad near Khairatabad/Saifabad, overlooking the southern end of Hussain Sagar lake - one of the Deccan's twin rocky hills, once known as 'Band Rock' where Mughal-to-Nizam proclamations were announced with music. The city below is Hyderabad, capital of Telangana.
